items.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
items.job: Replace internal water pump (timing cover removal), flush oil and coolant
items.note: If coolant has already damaged the bearings, an engine replacement runs $4,000–$7,000 or more.

items.t: Engine failure after coolant contamination or oil starvation
items.job: Replace engine with a used or remanufactured long block
items.note: Owners report an average of about $5,000 on CarComplaints.

items.t: AWD power transfer unit (PTU) leaks or fails
items.job: Replace PTU seals and fluid (whole unit if gears are damaged)
items.note: Seals and fluid are on the low end; a new or rebuilt PTU is on the high end.

items.t: Wheel bearing hum or growl
items.job: Replace wheel hub and bearing assembly (one corner)
items.note: Rusted-in hubs can add labor time.

items.t: Door ajar light stays on
items.job: Replace door latch assembly
items.note: Owners report about $300 on average.

items.t: Rear side window shatters on its own
items.job: Replace rear side window glass
items.note: Check your comprehensive insurance; glass claims often have a low deductible.

items.t: Front airbag may not fully inflate (recall)
items.job: Replace front airbag module
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Power steering assist can suddenly cut out (recall)
items.job: Update or replace electric power steering gear
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Fuel delivery module can crack and leak (recall)
items.job: Replace fuel delivery module
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Halfshaft can disengage and lose drive (recall)
items.job: Inspect and replace halfshaft/linkshaft
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Passenger airbag may switch off wrongly (recall)
items.job: Recalibrate or replace passenger occupant classification sensor
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Fuel pump can lose power and stall (recall)
items.job: Install fuel pump driver module fix
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Parking brake may not hold (recall)
items.job: Repair rear parking brake
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Turbo oil line can leak and cause a fire (recall)
items.job: Replace turbocharger oil supply line
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Rear toe link can break (recall)
items.job: Replace rear toe links
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Loose alternator or starter cables (recall)
items.job: Inspect and tighten alternator and starter cable nuts
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Rearview camera may show a blank screen (recall)
items.job: Update software or replace rearview camera
items.note: Free at a Ford dealer under the recall. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls.

items.t: Roof drain tubes clog and leak water inside
items.job: Clear, reconnect or reroute the roof glass drain tubes
items.note: No parts-and-labor source found, so this is based on owner-reported costs: TrueDelta Flex owners paid about $100–$350 to have plugged roof drains cleaned or rerun; CarComplaints lists a typical $350 for Flex roof leaks. Hours are worked back from those totals. Drying the interior or replacing water-damaged parts costs extra.

items.t: Clicking behind the dash from the blend door actuator
items.job: Replace the faulty HVAC blend door actuator
items.note: Parts: about $23 aftermarket (Four Seasons, fits 2009–2019 Flex) to $41–$82 list for Ford actuators, depending on which of the four failed. No stated labor time was found; hours are worked back from TrueDelta owner-reported totals of about $100–$600 (one dealer quote was $900). Some actuators are reachable under the dash, others take much more disassembly.

items.t: Electronic throttle body fault causes sudden power loss
items.job: Replace electronic throttle body and gasket, then do throttle relearn
items.note: go-parts lists about 1 hour of labor and $280–$526 shop labor; one owner was quoted $550 by Ford.

items.t: Cam timing codes and cold-start rattle from timing chain or phasers
items.job: Replace timing chain kit (chains, guides, tensioners; phasers if worn)
items.note: If only a cam timing (VCT) solenoid is stuck, the part is $30–$70 and the job is much shorter. go-parts puts a full timing job at about $2,000–$4,500; one owner was quoted $2,000+ and another paid $5,000 (TrueDelta).

items.t: Radiator cooling fan stops working and engine overheats
items.job: Replace engine cooling fan assembly or fan control module
items.note: go-parts lists about 1 hour; one owner on CarComplaints was quoted $685 parts plus $315 labor. YourMechanic average: about $671.
